transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-07-09
- Time: 15:00 UTC (approx)
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Owen (Redwood SE), Luis (CSM), Alex (CTO), Priya (Eng Lead), Benji (DevOps), Kara (Security)

Summary:
Quick integration immersion for HeliosChain's staging environment onboarding. Objectives: review connectivity and tenant mapping, clarify data residency/VPC options, agree load testing plan and pilot success criteria. Customer has a hybrid infra strategy and wants predictable latency under 200ms P50 for short prompt flows; also strong encryption/KMS requirements.

Topics covered:
- Staging topology and tenant isolation
- VPC peering vs egress proxy considerations
- Latency targets and batching tradeoffs
- Security controls (KMS, audit logs, SOC-2 ask)
- Pilot runbook and next steps

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Rivera: Okay, thanks everyone for joining, we've got about 45 mins. um, Priya and Benji from infra are with me. we want to make sure staging gets the right config so our ops team can validate performance before we flip to prod.
00:12 Maya Patel: Great, Alex. Thanks for the time. Quick intros — I'm Maya, I'll be your AE, Owen is our platform SE and will take most of the technical deep dive, and Luis from Customer Success will help with runbooks and ops cadence.
00:27 Owen Chen: Hi all. I'll jump into topology and then we'll look at traffic shaping and batching. quick note: some of my slides use the term "KV cache" — it's the same as session cache in older docs, sorry for the mix up.
00:40 Priya Shah: No worries. we've had different teams call the same thing different names; that's expected. two things up front: data residency — our EU customers need data to stay in eu-west, and encryption — we want KMS/HSM controls.
00:55 Owen Chen: Totally. For EU residency we can pin the staging region to eu-west-1; for private deploys we support customer-managed KMS. Kara, do you want to add specifics?
01:05 Kara Voss: Yes. We'll need envelope encryption with an external KMS key, rotation policies, and audit logging that shows key usage. also SSO/SAML attributes mapping for RBAC is required — we can share the SAML metadata after the call.
01:20 Maya Patel: Perfect — we'll attach our SSO walkthrough. Owen, can you talk through network options? they mentioned hybrid infra.
01:28 Owen Chen: Sure. Two common patterns: VPC peering / private endpoints for low-latency private traffic, or egress-proxied connections with NATs when peering isn't possible. For staging I usually recommend a private endpoint if you can — simpler ACLs and no NAT egress to cloud internet. That said, if you need cross-account constraints, an egress proxy is fine but watch for added latency jitter.
01:52 Benji Moore: If we do VPC peering what's the IP planning overhead? our current CIDR ranges are tight and we don't want overlap chaos.
02:00 Owen Chen: Yeah, good call. We can do a transit VPC or use AWS PrivateLink (if you're on AWS) to avoid CIDR collisions. we'll send a diagram with the options, and I can highlight the minimal routing changes.
02:12 Alex Rivera: On latency — our goal in staging is to validate we can hit ~200ms P50 on short questions (~40 token responses). what's realistic for your hosted offering vs a dedicated pool?
02:25 Owen Chen: For hosted lowest-latency bursts, we typically see P50s in the 80–150ms range for small responses on modern hardware when no batching. Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and lower tail latency under heavy load. But with batching you can trade off latency for cost — we can set max batch windows to keep P95s in bounds. we'll show a batching recommendation for your traffic profile.
02:45 Priya Shah: sounds good. we expect spikes during inbound dispatch windows — like 200QPS sustained for a 10-minute window. we'll upload a sample trace later.
02:56 Owen Chen: Perfect. That helps calibrate autoscale and instance counts. Also, caching prefixes — if you have repetitive prompts, prefix caching can reduce compute by 20–40% typically.
03:10 Luis Romero: From CS side, we'll provide an onboarding checklist and a runbook template. we try to include the exact verification steps: health endpoints, token validation, sample latency tests, and smoke evals.
03:24 Alex Rivera: Excellent. On compliance, we need an audit trail of prompt inputs and model selection decisions — possibly redaction rules. any built-in support for redaction or field-level obfuscation?
03:38 Owen Chen: We have post-processing hooks and filtering layers you can apply at the routing tier — we can redact sensitive PII before storage. for sensitive workloads we recommend not persisting full prompts; instead persist hashes or mask fields. Kara, does that align with your policy?
03:50 Kara Voss: Yes, our policy prefers non-persistent storage of raw PII and retention windows not longer than 30 days, with logs stored in an encrypted audit bucket. We'll need to review retention SLA language.
04:05 Maya Patel: We'll attach our retention and audit docs. quick note on rollouts: we support canary traffic and A/B routing, so you can validate on a subset before full swap.
04:18 Benji Moore: Good. For the staging environment, what's the easiest way to map tenants? we have multiple internal squads that need isolation.
04:27 Owen Chen: Two approaches: namespace tenancy where each tenant gets logical routing and separate model pinning, or shared runtime with tenant tags and tighter RBAC. For staging isolation, namespace tenancy is simpler — you'll get per-tenant metrics in the console.
04:42 Priya Shah: We'll probably want per-tenant metrics. I want to make sure costs don't explode though; can we set per-tenant quotas?
04:50 Maya Patel: Yes, rate limits and quotas are configurable. we can also give you token-level cost breakdowns in the console so you can attribute spend to teams.
05:02 Alex Rivera: Sounds like we need a pilot success definition. My thought: validate connectivity, run a 10-minute 200 QPS burst with no errors >1% and P50 <200ms, plus audit logs visible in S3. If those pass we move to production staging. Thoughts?
05:20 Owen Chen: That's reasonable. For the load test we recommend a soft ramp and one failover exercise to ensure fallbacks work. We'll provide a test harness script.
05:35 Luis Romero: I'll coordinate the runbook items and schedule the load window. Owen, you'll propose two time slots for the week of 7/20?
05:42 Owen Chen: Yup — I'll ping the calendar with options after the call.
05:46 Priya Shah: A few implementation gotchas from our side: we use an internal JWT scheme that overwrites the sub claim sometimes; we need to confirm token mapping in Redwood's request headers so we can trace per-user activity.
06:00 Owen Chen: We emit the original token-id in trace headers when configured; we can map that back to your JWT claim. we'll document the header names.
06:12 Benji Moore: Also curious about staging costs — any estimate for a 1-week pilot with 2 dedicated instances in eu-west handling that load?
06:20 Maya Patel: We can do a quick back-of-envelope and follow up with more precise pricing in the deck. For pilots we often use temporary dedicated capacity with an hourly estimate; I'll include sample numbers.
06:33 Alex Rivera: Any blockers on the security side we should know? Kara?
06:36 Kara Voss: Just the KMS integration and SAML mapping; we'll want to review the SOC 2 appendix and any penetration test results. please share redwood's latest security pack.
06:47 Maya Patel: We'll share SOC2 summary, pen test high-level, and our KMS integration guide. expect those in the email after this call.
06:56 Priya Shah: Great. One more — prompt templating: our front-end will do heavy templating client-side. is there a recommended approach to keep prompt size small and still preserve context?
07:07 Owen Chen: Use dynamic slotting instead of pasting full conversation history; rely on KV cache for long-lived sessions and only send deltas. We'll add a short best-practices doc for prompt size and cache TTLs.
07:22 Alex Rivera: OK — that's helpful. Let's summarize next steps.
07:27 Luis Romero: Recap: Redwood to share runbook, SSO guide, security pack, and pricing estimate by 7/13. Customer to upload sample prompts and traffic profile by 7/16. Owen to propose load test windows. Schedule the 1-hr load test for week of 7/20. Action owners in CRM.
07:50 Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and set the calendar invites. Appreciate the time.
07:56 Alex Rivera: Thanks all. bye.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription was decent but some technical terms (PrivateLink, KV cache) were occasionally transcribed inconsistently. There were a few overlaps and choppy sentences typical of conference calls.
